Package com.github.query4j.cache.impl

Class CacheStatisticsImpl

java.lang.Object
com.github.query4j.cache.impl.CacheStatisticsImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
CacheStatistics
public final class CacheStatisticsImpl extends Object implements CacheStatistics
Thread-safe implementation of cache statistics tracking.

Uses atomic operations for all counters to ensure thread-safety without synchronization overhead. Provides consistent snapshot views of cache performance metrics for monitoring and optimization.

All operations are lock-free and optimized for high-throughput concurrent access patterns typical in query caching scenarios.

Since:
1.0.0

  • Method Details

    • getHitCount

      public long getHitCount()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Returns the total number of cache hits since creation or last reset.

      A cache hit occurs when a requested key is found in the cache and has not expired. This metric indicates how often the cache successfully serves requests without database access.

      Specified by:
      getHitCount in interface CacheStatistics
      Returns:
      the hit count, always >= 0

    • getMissCount

      public long getMissCount()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Returns the total number of cache misses since creation or last reset.

      A cache miss occurs when a requested key is not found in the cache or has expired. This metric indicates how often requests must fall through to the database.

      Specified by:
      getMissCount in interface CacheStatistics
      Returns:
      the miss count, always >= 0

    • getEvictionCount

      public long getEvictionCount()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Returns the total number of cache evictions due to size or TTL limits.

      Evictions occur when:

      • The cache reaches its maximum size (size-based eviction)
      • Entries expire based on their TTL (time-based eviction)
      • Manual invalidation via CacheManager.invalidate(String)

      High eviction rates may indicate that cache size is too small or TTL is too short for the workload.

      Specified by:
      getEvictionCount in interface CacheStatistics
      Returns:
      the eviction count, always >= 0

    • getCurrentSize

      public long getCurrentSize()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Returns the current number of entries in the cache.

      This is a snapshot of the cache size at the time of the call and may change immediately in concurrent environments. The count includes all non-expired entries currently stored in memory.

      Specified by:
      getCurrentSize in interface CacheStatistics
      Returns:
      the current cache size, always >= 0

    • getMaxSize

      public long getMaxSize()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Returns the maximum configured size of the cache.

      This is the upper limit of entries the cache can hold before eviction begins. When the cache reaches this size, the least recently used (LRU) entries are evicted to make room for new entries.

      Specified by:
      getMaxSize in interface CacheStatistics
      Returns:
      the maximum size, or -1 if unbounded

    • getHitRatio

      public double getHitRatio()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Calculates and returns the cache hit ratio.

      The hit ratio is calculated as hits / (hits + misses), providing a value between 0.0 (no hits) and 1.0 (all hits). This is the primary metric for cache effectiveness.

      Target ratios:

      • > 0.80: Excellent - cache is highly effective
      • 0.60-0.80: Good - cache is working well
      • 0.40-0.60: Fair - consider tuning cache size or TTL
      • < 0.40: Poor - cache may not be beneficial
      Specified by:
      getHitRatio in interface CacheStatistics
      Returns:
      the hit ratio between 0.0 and 1.0, or 0.0 if no requests yet

    • getMissRatio

      public double getMissRatio()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Calculates and returns the cache miss ratio.

      The miss ratio is calculated as misses / (hits + misses), providing a value between 0.0 (no misses) and 1.0 (all misses). This is the complement of the hit ratio: missRatio = 1.0 - hitRatio.

      Specified by:
      getMissRatio in interface CacheStatistics
      Returns:
      the miss ratio between 0.0 and 1.0, or 1.0 if no hits yet

    • reset

      public void reset()
      Description copied from interface: CacheStatistics
      Resets all statistics counters to zero.

      This operation is thread-safe but may cause temporary inconsistencies in statistics during concurrent operations. Cache entries themselves are not affected - only the statistics counters are reset.

      Use this method when:

      • Starting a new monitoring period
      • After configuration changes to establish new baselines
      • During testing to isolate metrics for specific scenarios
      Specified by:
      reset in interface CacheStatistics
